clue.text: Scholar and man of letters

definitions.meaning: at Merton College, Oxford, a scholarship holder carries this title
one in charge of a post office, handling letters

explanation.definitionFit: Merton College calls its scholars by this title, and a post office head deals in mail, punning on a literary figure.

clue.text: Bears with expressions of contempt

definitions.meaning: Winnie-the-Pooh is the famous teddy bear, so several are bears
pooh is an exclamation of scorn

explanation.definitionFit: A. A. Milne's teddy gives a bear name, and the scornful exclamation gives disdainful remarks.

clue.text: Verlaine, for example, a sound percussion player

indicators.note: sound means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: one who plays cymbals

explanation.surface: The French poet, a decent drummer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a sound' looks like praise for the player but signals that the word is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul Verlaine was a leading poet of the late 19th-century French movement using suggestion and imagery.

clue.text: Duff gen causes error in motorway structure

indicators.note: the error is placed inside the motorway-plus-structure pair

parts.note: M1 is Britain's first motorway, read as MI
a formation is an arrangement or structure
a sin is a wrong, an error

explanation.surface: Bad information leads to a mistake in building the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: Duff is British slang for useless and gen for information; M1 is a London-to-Leeds motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: Duff means faulty and gen is facts, so faulty facts are false information.

clue.text: A poet's last words, keep recurring here

definitions.text: A poet's last words, keep recurring here

parts.words: A poet's last words, keep recurring here
parts.note: a verse form where the six line-ending words of the first stanza are reused in every stanza

explanation.surface: A dying poet's final words keep coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last words' suggests deathbed speech, but means the words ending each line.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fixed verse form of six stanzas reusing the same six end-words in rotation.

clue.text: Helen and Co turn out to be people of the same grade

indicators.note: turn out suggests the letters are rearranged into a new form

explanation.surface: Helen and her company prove to be equals.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank or level in an organisation, and the people at it.

clue.text: Woman married the first man to come along

definitions.text: the first man to come along

parts.note: Ada is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman wed the very first man who turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis he is the first human created, so literally the first man to appear.

clue.text: In French it's said to become the same

parts.note: dit is French for said

explanation.surface: In French, a saying becomes a cliche.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is used to mean as before, repeating what was said.

clue.text: It puts down explosive devices in the pit seam

parts.note: a pit is a mine
a seam of coal is a layer

explanation.surface: Something laying explosives in a coal seam.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that lays naval mines puts explosive charges in the sea.

clue.text: There is no point in this coarse piece

definitions.text: There is no point in this

parts.note: vulgar means coarse
a fraction is a piece or part

explanation.surface: A rude bit of writing is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: A fraction written as one number over another has no decimal point.
explanation.definitionFit: A common fraction like three-quarters is written without a decimal point.

clue.text: In the assimilation of ideas, master is gripped by two very big ones

indicators.note: something gripped is held inside, so the master letter goes within the pair of outsize marks
two signals that the outsize abbreviation is written twice in a row

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size for very big garments
M is an abbreviation for master, as in an MA degree

explanation.surface: In absorbing ideas, a teacher is held by two giants.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a clothing label, so 'very big ones' is a size tag rather than giants; 'two' writes it twice and 'gripped by' puts the master inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The word for gradual absorption through a membrane is used figuratively for soaking up knowledge without effort.

clue.text: No end of a game heavyweight in Texas:

indicators.note: the final letter of the game's name is dropped

parts.note: house, or housey-housey, is an old British name for bingo
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A heavyweight boxer playing an endless game somewhere in Texas.
explanation.walkthrough: HOUSE (bingo, in old British usage) loses its last letter to give HOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: The city is the largest one in that state, so it is found in Texas.

clue.text: To convey food to the beak, a shoveller is needed

parts.note: to spoon is to lift food with a spoon
a bird's bill is its beak

explanation.surface: A broad-billed bird needs its beak to scoop up food.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoveller is an old name for this wading bird with a flat, spatula-shaped bill.

clue.text: Malevolent spirit arising from lough

indicators.note: the answer comes up out of a rearrangement of the given word

explanation.surface: An evil spirit rising out of an Irish lake.
explanation.walkthrough: A lough is an Irish lake; its letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A ghoul is an evil spirit of folklore said to rob graves.

clue.text: Capital atmosphere in the firm

indicators.note: the word for atmosphere is placed inside the firm's abbreviation

parts.note: Co is short for company, a firm
air is the atmosphere around us

explanation.surface: The mood in the office is strictly business.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the seat of government of Egypt, a capital city.

clue.text: A post-natal service for women

parts.note: a church thanksgiving rite for mothers after giving birth, not a medical clinic

explanation.surface: A clinic for new mothers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a health clinic; it is a Christian rite of thanksgiving.
explanation.definitionFit: The ceremony gives thanks for a mother's safe delivery of a child.

clue.text: Briton may become distraught at such an irregularity

indicators.note: being distraught means being in disorder, so the letters are thrown about

explanation.surface: A Brit might get upset by such an oddity.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old form for a deformity or something departing from the norm.

clue.text: The issue is originality, of necessity

definitions.text: The issue is originality, of necessity

parts.words: The issue is originality, of necessity
parts.note: from the proverb that necessity is the mother of this, so it is necessity's issue, or child; it also means originality

explanation.surface: A remark that originality is inevitably the main point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' means offspring: the proverb makes necessity its mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Creativity, originality and the child of necessity in the proverb.

clue.text: Final demand from Thule Corporation

parts.note: Ultima Thule was the classical name for the furthest land north, so Thule suggests its partner word
corporation is an old jocular word for a paunch, a tum

explanation.surface: A last-chance letter arrives from a company called Thule.
explanation.walkthrough: Ultima Thule was the Roman name for the farthest land; corporation is old slang for a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a last set of terms whose rejection leads to a break or conflict.

clue.text: One expelled from Tube for causing damage

definitions.text: One expelled from Tube for causing damage

parts.words: One expelled from Tube for causing damage
parts.note: a weapon fired from a submarine's launch tube to wreck ships, not a vandal thrown off the London Underground

explanation.surface: A vandal thrown off the London Underground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is the London Underground, but here it is a launch tube.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-propelled underwater missile is fired from a tube to sink vessels.

clue.text: Broad knife with roughened surface protecting guerilla

indicators.note: the surface wraps around the guerrilla as if shielding him

parts.note: a matt surface is dull, not glossy
Che Guevara was the Argentine guerrilla leader

explanation.surface: A rough-handled blade carried by a rebel fighter.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant of machete, a broad cutting blade.

clue.text: Royals receive welcome from an uninhibited person

indicators.note: the royals take in the greeting, so it goes between them

parts.note: R for Rex or Regina, twice for two royals
ave is Latin for hail, a greeting

explanation.surface: The royal couple are greeted by a wild partygoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild, partying person who lets loose is called this in British slang.

clue.text: Sandhurst may give him the pip

definitions.text: Sandhurst may give him the pip

parts.words: Sandhurst may give him the pip
parts.note: Sandhurst is Britain's officer academy; a pip is the star on a junior officer's shoulder, though 'give the pip' means annoy

explanation.surface: The military academy irritates one of its students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give the pip' is British for annoy, but a pip is also the star an officer trainee earns on commissioning.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainee at the officer academy who is awarded the rank star on passing out.

clue.text: Remove from container in warehouse?

definitions.meaning: to ... is to take a plant out of its pot

explanation.definitionFit: Read as de-pot it means to take out of a plant pot; as one word it is a storehouse.

clue.text: In Crete, church orders the maintenance of silence

indicators.note: to order is to arrange, so the letters are set out again

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church in Crete insists on keeping quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link setting the scene in Crete, but it is part of what 'orders' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint in speech, keeping one's thoughts to oneself, is this quality.

clue.text: Nobleman beginning to yawn before time

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman

indicators.note: the first letter of the next word is wanted

explanation.surface: A lord starts yawning before it is time.
explanation.definitionFit: Ahead of the expected hour, premature.

clue.text: Better confess to parking by range

parts.note: to confess is to own up: I'm guilty
P is the sign for parking
to range is to wander, rove

explanation.surface: Admitting to parking near the cooker is an improvement.
explanation.definitionFit: To get better is to make progress, a verb sense.

clue.text: More daring musical — that's the first sign of realism!

parts.note: Hair is the 1960s rock musical
i.e. stands for id est, that is

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: A bolder stage show — at last, a hint of realism.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairy means risky, so this comparative is riskier, more daring.

clue.text: Not a broadcasting centre — a Philistine place

definitions.text: Not a broadcasting centre — a Philistine place

parts.words: Not a broadcasting centre — a Philistine place
parts.note: alludes to David's lament 'Tell it not in ...', so news was not to be spread in this Philistine city

explanation.surface: A Philistine town that is no media hub.
explanation.walkthrough: In 2 Samuel, David says 'Tell it not in ...' of this Philistine city, so news is not broadcast there.
explanation.definitionFit: It was one of the five Philistine cities, home of Goliath.

clue.text: Specs worn by the funny nursemaid for the folk-singing

indicators.note: spectacles are worn on a face, so these go inside the jumbled letters
funny means odd, so the letters of the word are mixed up

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of spectacles
a nanny is a nursemaid

explanation.surface: A nanny in silly glasses leads the sing-along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'funny' looks like it describes the nursemaid, but it scrambles the word before it; 'worn by' puts the specs inside, as glasses sit on a face.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an informal gathering for folk music and dancing, a folk-song party.
